title: Support `<selectedcontent>` in `<select multiple>`
body: This PR adds support for the selectedcontent element in a select element with the multiple attribute. Every option in the select's list of options is cloned into selectedcontent, and each clone has the same selectedness as the option it was cloned from. A new UA style rule hides the clones which aren't selected: ```css select[multiple] selectedcontent > option:not(:checked) { display: none; } ``` Here is what the markup would look like after the selectedcontent element performs its cloning: ```html ``` The clones are not considered options of the select, and the UA style rules which give options their size, spacing, layout, and interactive styles exclude them with `:not(selectedcontent > option)`. Since every option insertion means selectedcontent needs updating, the options are only cloned at these times: - **When the select is done being parsed.** Nothing is cloned and no microtasks are queued during parsing, because microtask timing relative to parsing is inconsistent, which would make the clone timing and mutation records inconsistent. - **In a microtask coalesced per select, when modified by script.** This avoids cloning every option each time an option is inserted when building a select imperatively. Changing an option's selectedness updates the selectedness of its existing clone without re-cloning.
